question: Which body system uses chemical messengers (hormones) to drive all the body changes during puberty?
explanation: Spot on! The endocrine system is our body's hormone-manufacturing network, releasing chemical messengers straight into the bloodstream to spark growth and development. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h1)

question: Before puberty starts, what does the central nervous system usually do regarding reproductive hormones?

options.B: It completely shuts down the pituitary

explanation: You got it! Throughout childhood, the brain actively keeps reproductive hormone levels low and quiet until the body is mature enough for puberty. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which tiny brain structure sits right at the top of the HPG hormone axis command chain?
explanation: Great job! The hypothalamus acts as the ultimate master control center in the brain, heading up the HPG axis. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h2)

question: In a female body, which organs make up the 'gonads' part of the HPG axis?
explanation: Spot on! Gonads are the primary reproductive organs—testes in males and ovaries in females. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h2)

question: How must Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) be released to properly wake up the pituitary gland?
explanation: You nailed it! GnRH loves a rhythmic beat. It has to be released in pulses; if it flows constantly in a steady stream, hormone production actually shuts down. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h3)

question: Where in the body is Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) originally manufactured?
explanation: Correct! Special nerve cells tucked inside the hypothalamus build and release GnRH to kickstart the whole reproductive cascade. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h3)

question: Which gland gets the message from GnRH and then releases LH and FSH into the bloodstream?
explanation: Well done! The anterior pituitary gland acts on the hypothalamus's command to synthesize and pump out both LH and FSH. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h4)

question: Once Luteinizing Hormone (LH) finally reaches the gonads, what is its main job?

options.C: It stops the secretion of GnRH
options.D: It triggers immediate linear height growth

explanation: Spot on! LH targets specific cells in the gonads to prompt the creation of powerhouse sex hormones like testosterone and estrogen. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h4)

question: When LH travels to the male testes, which specific cells step up to produce testosterone?
explanation: You got it! Leydig cells are the testosterone factories inside the testes, working hard when triggered by LH. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h5)

question: What is the proper term for the biological process of making mature sperm cells during male puberty?
explanation: Awesome! 'Spermatogenesis' simply means the creation (-genesis) of sperm, fueled by FSH and testosterone. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h5)

question: What is the primary and most potent estrogen produced by the ovaries during female puberty?
explanation: Spot on! Estradiol is the heavy-hitter estrogen that drives female secondary sexual development. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h6)

question: How does estrogen impact a growing teenager's height during puberty?

options.A: It only lengthens the bones of the arms and legs without stopping
options.B: It permanently prevents any linear height growth from occurring
options.C: It has no effect on skeletal development or bone length
options.D: It accelerates bone growth but also causes early closure of growth plates

explanation: You nailed it! Estrogen gives teens a fast growth spurt at first, but it also signals the growth plates to eventually fuse and close up. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h6)

question: Which of these options is NOT a secondary sexual characteristic?
explanation: Correct! The uterus and ovaries are primary sex organs (we are born with them), while secondary characteristics develop later on the outside. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h7)

question: Why do many teenagers suddenly struggle with acne and body odor during puberty?

options.A: Increased hormone activity stimulates sweat and oil glands
options.B: Dietary habits change completely during the teenage years
options.C: The lymphatic system becomes temporarily blocked by growth
options.D: Skin cells stop shedding their outer protective layers

explanation: Spot on! Surging hormones wake up our sebaceous (oil) and sweat glands, leading to extra oil and body odor. Totally normal part of growing up! [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h7)

question: What is the medical term for when a child starts going through puberty much earlier than normal?
explanation: Great job! 'Precocious' means developing certain talents or traits earlier than expected—in this case, early puberty. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h8)

question: A 14-year-old boy shows no physical signs of testicular enlargement or puberty yet. How would a nurse document this finding?
explanation: You got it! When physical maturation hasn't started by age 14 in males, it is clinically categorized as delayed puberty. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h8)
